description: The gravitational field bodies fall in.

x-enumDescriptions.Pairwise: Every source-target interaction, the exact deterministic oracle.
x-enumDescriptions.FastMonopole: An adaptive octree whose accepted distant cells contribute their total mass at their centre of mass.
x-enumDescriptions.AdaptiveFmm: An adaptive dual-tree fast multipole solve with first-order Cartesian local expansions.

gravitationalConstant.description: The non-negative proportionality constant applied to every source mass.

softeningLength.description: The positive Plummer softening length that bounds the force at short range.

attractors.description: The static sources, or empty for a field summed from bodies alone.

items.description: One gravitational source the world declares, riding a placement's authored transform.

placementId.description: The placements row whose position the source sits at. The row need not be solid or visible; only its transform is read.

items.title: WorldGravityAttractor

uniform.description: A constant acceleration added to every solved answer, in world units per second squared. Point masses cannot express a uniform field, so this is how a world keeps a flat floor underfoot while its attractors own the space around them: authored as an acceleration, it is already what a body integrates.

points.description: Ergonomic point/planet presets lowered to static masses through the same Plummer kernel as Attractors. Absent means none.

items.description: A point-gravity preset riding a placement, authored in the quantities a world designer observes.

placementId.description: The placements row at the point source's centre.

surfaceGravity.description: The positive acceleration magnitude, in world units per second squared, promised at ReferenceRadius after the world's authored softening is applied.

referenceRadius.description: The positive distance from the source centre at which SurfaceGravity is promised. For a planet this is its surface radius; a source need not carry geometry.

items.title: WorldGravityPoint

areas.description: Bounded placement-relative influences evaluated after the global solve. Absent means none.

items.description: A bounded local gravity influence riding a placement's resolved transform.

placementId.description: The placement whose position, yaw, scale, and optional body attachment the area follows.

priority.description: The deterministic composition priority. Lower values apply first; authored order breaks ties, so a later equal-priority row applies later.

mode.description: Whether the matching area's acceleration combines with or replaces the accumulated answer.
mode.title: WorldGravityAreaMode

x-enumDescriptions.Combine: Add the area's acceleration to the accumulated global and lower-priority answer.
x-enumDescriptions.Replace: Replace the accumulated answer with the area's acceleration. A zero directional vector creates a deliberate zero-gravity pocket.

bounds.description: The placement-relative analytic bound. Boundary points are included.

anyOf.description: A sphere centered on the riding placement.

radius.description: The positive placement-local radius, multiplied by the placement's scale.

anyOf.title: WorldGravityAreaBoundsSphereBounds

anyOf.description: A yaw-oriented box centered on the riding placement.

halfExtents.description: The positive placement-local half extents, multiplied by the placement's scale.

anyOf.title: WorldGravityAreaBoundsBoxBounds

bounds.title: WorldGravityAreaBounds

anyOf.description: A placement-local acceleration vector, rotated by the placement's resolved yaw.

value.description: The acceleration vector in world units per second squared. Zero is admitted so Replace can author a zero-gravity pocket. An area's Vector rows, where authored, supply the vector in its place.

anyOf.title: WorldGravityAreaAccelerationDirectional

anyOf.description: A constant-magnitude acceleration directed toward the placement origin.

magnitude.description: The nonzero signed acceleration magnitude in world units per second squared.

anyOf.title: WorldGravityAreaAccelerationRadial

anyOf.description: A constant-magnitude acceleration directed toward the line through the placement origin along Axis: the pull of a cylinder, or with a negative magnitude the hold of a tube's inside.

magnitude.description: The nonzero signed acceleration magnitude in world units per second squared.

axis.description: The line's placement-local direction, rotated by the placement's resolved yaw. Absent is the placement's own Y axis.

anyOf.title: WorldGravityAreaAccelerationAxial

anyOf.description: A constant-magnitude acceleration directed toward the plane through the placement origin, from either side of it: the pull of a slab a body walks on both faces of.

magnitude.description: The nonzero signed acceleration magnitude in world units per second squared.

normal.description: The plane's placement-local normal, rotated by the placement's resolved yaw. Absent is the placement's own Y axis.

anyOf.title: WorldGravityAreaAccelerationPlanar

anyOf.description: An acceleration toward the placement origin that falls with distance as a uniform ball's does: SurfaceGravity at ReferenceRadius, the inverse square of the distance beyond it, and in proportion to the distance inside it.

surfaceGravity.description: The nonzero signed acceleration at the reference radius.

referenceRadius.description: The positive distance from the origin at which the surface value holds, multiplied by the placement's scale.

anyOf.title: WorldGravityAreaAccelerationPointMass

anyOf.description: A constant-magnitude acceleration toward the nearest solid surface: against the world contact field's gradient at the body, so a body walks on whatever shape the world's solids give the field. The world must select gradient-derived up (GradientDerivedUp), which is what makes its contact provider answer the gradient.

magnitude.description: The nonzero signed acceleration magnitude in world units per second squared.

anyOf.title: WorldGravityAreaAccelerationSurface

blend.description: The depth inside the bound, in world units, over which the area's weight rises smoothly from nothing at the bound to one. Zero, the default, gives the area its whole weight everywhere inside. At a weight between the two a Replace area mixes its answer with the accumulated one in that proportion and a Combine area adds that share of its own, so a body passing between two areas turns across the depth and never in one tick.

weight.description: A Fixed state row whose value, clamped to zero through one, multiplies the area's weight: zero takes the area out of the fold altogether. Absent is one.

scale.description: A Fixed state row whose signed value multiplies the area's acceleration: minus one turns the pull about. Absent is one.

vector.description: Three Fixed state rows that supply a Directional area's placement-local vector in place of the authored one. Each is a row of its own so each may be a followed row: another world's value, read here as gravity.

x.description: The Fixed slot row holding the vector's placement-local x.

y.description: The Fixed slot row holding the vector's placement-local y.

z.description: The Fixed slot row holding the vector's placement-local z.

vector.title: WorldGravityAreaVector

items.title: WorldGravityArea

orbits.description: Closed-form orbits, each about a placement. Absent means none.

items.description: A closed-form orbit about a placement: a conic whose phase is an exact fraction of the engine tick, so its position at any tick is computed directly and never by stepping the ticks before it.

name.description: The orbit's name, unique in the section.

around.description: The placement at the orbit's focus. One attached to a body follows that body, so an orbit nests about a body riding another.

semiMajorAxis.description: The positive semi-major axis, in world units.

periodSeconds.description: The positive period, an exact whole number of engine ticks.

eccentricity.description: The eccentricity, zero for a circle and below MaxEccentricity.

inclinationDegrees.description: The tilt of the orbit's plane from the world's XZ plane, about its line of nodes.

ascendingNodeDegrees.description: The heading of the line of nodes about +Y from +X.

periapsisDegrees.description: The angle in the plane from the line of nodes to the periapsis.

phase.description: The fraction of a turn past the periapsis at engine tick zero.

bodyIndex.description: The population body that rides the orbit, or absent for an orbit nothing rides.

riding.description: A state row whose nonzero value keeps the body on the orbit. Absent rides always.

joinSpeed.description: The speed, in world units per second, at which a body away from the orbit closes on it once it rides again, on top of the orbit's own motion: it catches the rails rather than jumping onto them. Zero, the default, puts the body on the orbit at once.

items.title: WorldGravityOrbit

tides.description: Far sources whose pull reaches the world as a tide. Absent means none.

items.description: A far mass whose pull reaches this world as a tide: the difference of its pull across the world, since the pull itself moves the world's frame with everything in it and is dropped.

surfaceGravity.description: The positive acceleration the source would give at ReferenceRadius from its centre, in world units per second squared. With the radius it states the source's mass in the quantities a designer observes.

referenceRadius.description: The positive distance from the source's centre at which SurfaceGravity holds.

placementId.description: The placement at the source's centre, in this world's frame. Exactly one of this and Orbit is authored.

orbit.description: The orbit whose position is the source's centre.

scale.description: A Fixed state row whose value multiplies the source's mass: a followed row carries another world's mass here, and zero is a source that has gone. Absent is one.

items.title: WorldGravityTide

tideOrigin.description: The placement the tide is formed at: the point of the world that falls freely with the far sources' pull. Absent is the world's origin.

isActive.description: Gets a value indicating whether the section declares an active global or bounded local field, an orbit or a tide.

title: WorldGravity
